definition: A method for aggregating multiple model outputs by selecting the answer that appears most frequently among several independently generated responses.
details: Majority voting, closely related to self-consistency, is a simple but effective way to improve accuracy on tasks with a single correct answer by leveraging agreement across multiple sampled reasoning attempts.
story: Think of a jazz musician who has heard so many solos that a new one simply falls out of their fingers. Given a starting line, the machine imagines what comes next — a word, a note, a patch of a picture. It makes new things by recombining everything it has ever seen. Creation, here, is memory recombined at speed. That next-word, next-stroke magic is Majority Voting.
